_comment: Single source of truth for routing + escalation. build_workflow.py inlines this into the 'Route & Escalate' Code node. Edit here, then rebuild.

llm._comment: llama-3.3-70b-versatile returned model_not_found for a free-tier key (Sept 2026). gpt-oss-120b is the strongest model available on the free tier; reasoning_effort=low keeps latency and tokens down for a short classification task. Set reasoning_effort to null for non-reasoning models (e.g. Ollama).

queues.engineering: Engineering - product defects affecting one customer or feature
queues.incident_response: SRE / on-call - service-wide unavailability or degradation
queues.billing: Billing & Finance - invoices, charges, contract rates
queues.product: Product Management - feature requests and roadmap input
queues.technical_support: Solutions / Support Engineering - how-to, configuration, integration questions
queues.human_review_escalation: Human triage lead - anything flagged by an escalation rule or failed processing

_escalate_multi_intent_comment: Escalate when the classifier reports a separate request in another category (secondary_categories non-empty). One ticket can't sit in two queues; a human splits it.

thresholds._billing_threshold_basis_options: any_amount (chosen) = escalate a Billing Issue if any dollar amount in the message exceeds the threshold; discrepancy = only if (largest - smallest amount) exceeds it. 'Either' collapses to any_amount because the discrepancy can never exceed the largest amount. Message #3: $1,240 vs $980 -> escalates under any_amount, not under discrepancy ($260).

keywords._comment: Matched case-insensitively on word boundaries against the raw message. Deliberately narrow: bare words like 'everyone' or 'all users' were left out because they appear in feature requests ('everyone on my team wants...').

_security_signal_comment: Access-failure terms only. A mere mention of SSO/login (e.g. a how-to question) is not a signal. Policy: raise priority to High and record the rule, but do not escalate on its own.
